title: The rushed meeting notes
explanation: The fix cuts one big job into four small ones and asks to see each result. Each step uses the one before, and you can check each one. Options A and C ask for care or detail, but still pile everything into one go.
brokenPrompt: Read these notes from our club meeting, write the summary, pick the three most important actions, give each one to a person, and write a reminder email for each person.
brokenOutput:
Summary: The club met and talked about several things.
Actions: Do the things.
Dear all, please remember the actions. Thanks.

diagnoses.text: The assistant is not able to write emails.
Four big jobs were packed into one order, so each one got only a little attention.
The order was not polite enough.

wrongDiagnosisHint: Count how many separate jobs the order asks for at once.
rightDiagnosisNote: The order asked for four jobs in one go. The assistant rushed through all four and did none of them well.

fixes.prompt: Please do all four of these jobs carefully and do not rush: the summary, the actions, the owners, and the reminders.

Do this in steps. Step 1: summarise the notes in three sentences. Step 2: list the three most important actions. Step 3: give each action to a person named in the notes. Step 4: write a one-line reminder for each person. Show each result before the next step.
Do all four jobs in one long answer, and make it as detailed as you can.

wrongFixHint: Asking it not to rush is not a plan. Pick the one that splits the job into numbered steps.
fixedOutput:
Step 1 (summary): The club will run a plant sale on 14 May. We need posters, plants, and helpers.
Step 2 (actions): 1. Make posters. 2. Collect plants. 3. Recruit helpers.
Step 3 (owners): Posters: Dara. Plants: Mei. Helpers: Tomas.
Step 4 (reminders): Dara, please finish the posters by Friday. Mei, please collect the plants by Saturday. Tomas, please recruit three helpers by Monday.
